chunks: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I have suffered severe distress from the whispering in my chest, and I am a man with dependents, in debt, and in need.” So he said to him:

“Repeat these words: ‘I place my trust in the Ever-Living who does not die,’ and ‘All praise is for Allah, who has not taken a consort nor a child, and there is no partner for Him in the kingdom, and there is no protector for Him out of weakness; and magnify Him greatly.’”
He said: It was not long before the man returned to him and said: “O Messenger of Allah, Allah has removed the whispering from my chest, settled my debt, and expanded my sustenance.”

key_terms.الْحَيِّ: the Ever-Living, one of the divine attributes of Allah
key_terms.تَوَكَّلْتُ: I placed my trust and reliance in Allah
key_terms.شَرِيكٌ: a partner or associate in dominion, negated from Allah
key_terms.مُحْوِجٌ: in a state of need and poverty
key_terms.مُعِيلٌ: a person responsible for supporting dependents
key_terms.وَسْوَسَةِ: inner whispering or troubling thoughts in the chest

ai.seo_question: What du'a did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله teach for anxiety, debt, and constricted sustenance?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a supplication taught by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله to a man suffering from inner whisperings, debt, and hardship. The supplication combines tawakkul in Allah with words of tawhid drawn from the Qur'an, and the narration presents it as a means for relief from distress and expansion of provision.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.986 - Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"A man came to the Prophet (sw) and said:
'O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), I am experiencing great distress due to the whispers in my chest, and I am a man who is a caretaker, in debt, and in need.'
The Prophet (sw) said to him: 'Repeat these words:
"I place my trust in the Ever-Living, Who does not die," and "Praise be to Allah (swt), Who did not take a wife or a son, and Who has no partner in His kingdom, nor a helper in His humiliation," and magnify Him with great magnification.'
The man said that shortly afterward, he returned to the Prophet (sw) and said:
'O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), Allah (swt) has removed the whispers from my chest, settled my debt, and expanded my sustenance.'"
